hooks.prompt: Phase 0 mesh verification (shepherd issue #23). The just-edited file is a sprint plan. (1) Read tool_input.file_path. (2) Read the file. (3) Grep for 'landed in tree' / 'confirmed at' / 'in tree:' phrasing paired with a file path + symbol reference. (4) For each claim, run: git merge-base HEAD origin/main (fallback origin/master, HEAD~20) to get base; then git log --oneline <base>..HEAD -- <referenced-file>. If the referenced symbol does not appear in any commit message or diff for that file, mark unverified. (5) Respond {"ok": true} if all claims verified, or if no 'landed in tree' claims found, or if sprint base cannot be resolved. Otherwise {"ok": false, "reason": "Phase 0 mesh: N claim(s) unverified vs sprint git log: <list>. False 'landed' claims propagate to next session as ground truth (issue #23). Verify each landed claim with git log <base>..HEAD -- <file> before writing the plan."}. Max 10 tool calls. Be terse.

(3) Grep for 'landed in tree' / 'confirmed at' / 'in tree:' phrasing paired with a file path + symbol reference. (4) For each claim, run: git merge-base HEAD origin/main (fallback origin/master, HEAD~20) to get base; then git log --oneline <base>..HEAD -- <referenced-file>. (5) Respond {"ok": true} if all claims verified, or if no 'landed in tree' claims found, or if sprint base cannot be resolved. Wave-gate cherry-pick verification (shepherd issue #21). Fast-path: (1) Run: git branch 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^  agent-' || echo 0. If 0, respond {"ok": true} immediately and use no further tools. Heavy path (only if agent-* branches exist): (2) Get sprint branch via git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD. (3) For each agent-* branch: run git rev-list --right-only --count "<sprint>...<branch>" 2>/dev/null. Collect branches whose count > 0 (stray commits not in sprint). (4) If none stray, respond {"ok": true}. (5) Else respond {"ok": false, "reason": "WAVE-GATE: N agent branch(es) have unique commits not in <sprint>: <list of branch:count>. Cherry-pick onto sprint before closing the wave (issue #21). Silent data-loss risk if next session inherits 'complete' from plan/handoff while commits remain orphaned."}. Max 5 tool calls. Default to ok=true on any error. Be terse.

Close-finalize completion check (shepherd GH #60; false-positive fix #122/#127). Require TWO independent positive signals before flagging incomplete. (1) Run: git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null. If HEAD does NOT match *-dev.[0-9]*, respond {"ok": true} — not in a sprint context. (2) Subworktree guard: compare output of git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null with pwd. If they differ, respond {"ok": true} — worktree creation refreshes mtimes on historical close reports; skip check. (3) BRANCH = branch name from step 1. Derive sprint slug: strip leading 'v', collapse version dots, e.g. v0.3.4-dev.9 → slug '034-dev9'. (4) Signal A — close report committed in git (do NOT use mtime or find): run git log --oneline --diff-filter=A --all -- "*${slug}*close*.md" 2>/dev/null | head -1. If empty → respond {"ok": true} (no committed close report for this sprint; sprint still in progress). (5) Signal B — sprint branch still on origin: git ls-remote --heads origin "${BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null | head -1. If empty → respond {"ok": true} (branch already gone from origin; finalize complete). (6) Both signals positive (committed close report found AND sprint branch still on origin): respond {"ok": false, "reason": "CLOSE-FINALIZE INCOMPLETE: close report committed for ${BRANCH} but sprint branch still present on origin. Verify dev→patch merge: git log origin/<patch_branch>..${BRANCH} --oneline should be empty if merged. Then run conductor §CLOSE-FINALIZE steps 4–6 via explicit operator-confirmed commands."}. Max 4 tool calls. Default ok=true on any error or ambiguity. Be terse.
